stories.title: Integrating GC-MS compositional profiling with ATR-FTIR spectral fingerprinting of Melissa officinalis L. and Thymus vulgaris L. essential oils obtained by supercritical CO2 extraction
stories.description: Essential oils of Melissa officinalis L. (lemon balm) and Thymus vulgaris L. (common thyme) are valued for antioxidant, antimicrobial and antispasmodic bioactivities linked to their monoterpenoid and phenolic content. In this study, oils were isolated from dried leaves by supercritical carbon dioxide extraction (SC-CO2; 40 °C, 10 MPa) and benchmarked against conventional n-hexane maceration, then characterized in parallel by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR, 4000–400 cm⁻¹). Triplicate independent extractions (three extraction batches per species, each prepared from a single commercial plant batch and analysed once) gave yields (mean ± SD) of 0.90 ± 0.03% (SFE) and 1.03 ± 0.07% (n-hexane) for M. officinalis, and 0.97 ± 0.03% and 0.95 ± 0.04% for T. vulgaris. Yields of the two methods did not differ significantly for either species (Welch’s t-test, p = 0.068 for M. officinalis and p = 0.53 for T. vulgaris), although with three replicates per group these tests have little power and cannot establish equivalence of the methods. GC-MS resolved the T. vulgaris oil as a thymol/γ-terpinene/p-cymene chemotype (23.0%, 29.0% and 20.3% of normalized peak area, respectively; raw means 22.4 ± 0.4%, 28.1 ± 1.1% and 19.8 ± 0.2%) and the M. officinalis oil as a geranial/neral/geranyl acetate profile (23.9 ± 0.3%, 22.5 ± 0.6% and 18.6 ± 0.7%). All percentages derive from manually re-integrated chromatograms (per-replicate resolved-area totals 95.5–99.7% for T. vulgaris and 95.5–97.5% for M. officinalis). All GC-MS percentages are area-normalized, semi-quantitative relative abundances obtained without compound-specific calibration and, owing to partial co-elution among the major monoterpene hydrocarbons, should be regarded as approximate. ATR-FTIR spectra corroborated these compositions: the composite aromatic C–H wagging band at ~ 808 cm⁻¹ in thyme oil scaled with the combined thymol/p-cymene/γ-terpinene aromatic load, while the 1671 cm⁻¹ α,β-unsaturated carbonyl band in lemon balm oil tracked the pooled geranial/neral fraction. Spectral correlation coefficients between SFE and n-hexane extracts were ≥ 0.99 for both species, consistent with closely similar bulk chemical selectivity of the two non-polar media; because GC-MS was applied only to the SC-CO2 extracts, this similarity refers to bulk spectral fingerprints rather than compound-resolved composition. Under the mild condition tested (40 °C, 10 MPa), SC-CO2 extraction retained the diagnostic chemotype of both species. Once anchored to GC-MS reference data, ATR-FTIR fingerprinting may therefore serve as a rapid, solvent-minimal, chromatography-free screening tool for chemotype assessment and essential oil quality control; this application should be regarded as preliminary until it has been tested on independent samples covering different geographical origins, production batches and chemotypes.

stories.title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
stories.description: The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments. We show how a parasite can manage to maintain its remarkable swimming capabilities while it infests diverse tissue spaces in vertebrate bodies. We show in 3D how the flagellated cell body flexibly adjusts in response to divers confinement conditions.

stories.title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
stories.description: Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics. A nanotwinned tantalum nitride ceramic combines transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity, enabling up to 60% compressive strain while retaining high hardness (~43 GPa). This offers a route to developing strong, damage-tolerant ceramics.

stories.title: Background gravitational waves as signature of the accelerated cosmic expansion.
stories.description: We propose a toy model of a spherical universe made up of an exotic dark gas with temperature T in thermal equilibrium with a black-body in adiabatic expansion. Each particle of this exotic gas mimics a kind of particle of dark energy. So, each dark particle occupies a very small area of space so-called Planck area L p 2 , which represents the minimum area of the whole space-time given by the spherical surface with area 4 π R H 2 , where R H is the Hubble radius. We realize that such spherical surface is the surface of the black-body for representing the dark universe as if it were the surface of an expanding balloon. Thus, we are able to derive the law of universal gravitation, thus leading us to understand the cosmological anti-gravity. We estimate the tiny order of magnitude of the cosmological constant and the acceleration of expansion of the dark sphere. In this toy model, as the dark universe can be thought of as a large black body, when we obtain its power and frequency of emission of radiation, we find very low values. We conclude that such radiation and frequency of the black body made up of dark energy is a background gravitational wave with very low frequency in the order of 1 0 − 1 7 Hz due to the slight stretching of the fabric of space-time. [ABSTRACT FROM AUTHOR]
